parts.name: reef_board
parts.notes: Hexagonal limestone slab. bbox x=238mm is MY READING of idea.json's '~238mm across the flats' as the board's overall CORNER-TO-CORNER (vertex-to-vertex) span rather than the literal flat-to-flat measurement the phrase names (see unstated_in_spec) -- this is the one reading consistent with the board's own pitch/ring/pan-size numbers: a 3-ring (37-pan) hex-of-hexes at 34mm pitch reaches a pan CENTRE 3x34=102mm from the board centre along each of 6 corner directions, and a 30mm-across-flats pan has its own 17.3mm circumradius, so the outermost vertex sits at 102+17.3=119.3mm from centre -- doubled, 238.6mm, matching the stated figure almost exactly. The literal flat-to-flat reading would instead put the CORNER-to-corner span at 238/(sqrt(3)/2)=274.8mm, which fails the 246mm bed in every rotation (verified: the best-case minimal bounding square over all rotations is 265mm) and contradicts idea.json's own 'Fits the P2S bed in one piece' -- so the corner-to-corner reading is also the only one that keeps that claim true. bbox y=206mm is MY COMPUTATION of the derived flat-to-flat width from the 238mm corner-to-corner figure (238 x sqrt(3)/2 = 206.1mm, standard hexagon geometry, mirroring millbind's precedent of deriving the missing perpendicular hex dimension). bbox z=14mm is idea.json's own stated figure, used directly. 37 hexagonal tide pans on a triangular lattice at 34mm pitch (centre, ring of 6, ring of 12, ring of 18 = 1+6+12+18=37, idea.json's own figures) -- OWNS the 34mm pan pitch and the 30mm pan across-flats width; nothing else in the brief restates either number. Each pan is a 30mm-across-flats, 3mm-deep hexagonal dish with 1.2mm ripple relief on its floor, indexing an urchin_shell's 29mm hex footprint to one of six 60-degree orientations with the stated ~0.5mm clearance per side (0.5mm derives directly and exactly from the stated 30mm dish over the stated 29mm shell -- (30-29)/2=0.5mm, no invention). Each pan also carries a 6.6mm-diameter, 10mm-deep socket at its exact centre for a pearl shaft -- this is a peg-only engagement (only the pearl's 6mm shaft enters; the 16mm knob rests above the pan surface) and is captured entirely through the `joins` interfaces below, never as a `recesses` entry, because the recesses formula measures against the held piece's WIDEST footprint (the 16mm knob) and would wrongly fail a socket sized only for the 6mm shaft (mirrors millbind's yard_board pin-through-bore precedent, which excluded its own post/bore engagement from `recesses` for the identical reason). The 19 inner pans (centre plus the first two rings) carry a 1.2mm raised collar and are the SEED PANS; the 6 corner pans of the outer ring carry a 1.5mm raised barnacle cluster and are the LANDING SHELVES -- both idea.json's own stated relief figures. relief_mm=1.2mm is the shallowest of the board's three relief features (1.2mm floor ripple, 1.2mm seed collar, 1.5mm landing barnacle), so 1.2mm is the binding value reported here (same practice as millbind's yard_board). Single tile -- 238x206x14mm is well inside the 246x246x251mm P2S bed once read as corner-to-corner (see above); no `joins`/tiling needed anywhere in this brief.

parts.name: urchin_shell
parts.notes: Domed hexagonal carapace, 29mm across the flats (idea.json's stated figure, used directly for bbox x/y) with 1.2mm radial grooves fanning across the dome (idea.json's stated relief figure). Total standalone height (bbox z=34mm) is MY ADDITIVE READING of two figures idea.json states as separate features rather than a combined total: the dome body is '~18mm tall' and the central grip knob 'rises ~16mm for lifting' out of the dome's crown -- I read the knob as standing further proud OF the 18mm dome (18+16=34mm) rather than being subsumed within it, since it is introduced as a further lifting feature rising out of an already-specified dome height (see unstated_in_spec). Six sockets, 6.6mm diameter and 12mm deep, sunk vertically at the six face centres on a ~11mm radius (all idea.json's own stated figures) -- deep enough that spines and pearls stay seated when the shell is lifted upright for a TURN or CREEP. A central grip knob 12mm across, 16mm of that rise counted into the 34mm total above. The grip knob's prism carries three, four, five or six flats -- a player's identity for the game, read by counting edges. No `recesses` block: like reef_board's pearl sockets, these six sockets receive only a 6mm peg (spine) or 6mm shaft (pearl), never the piece's full body, so the engagement is captured entirely through the `joins` interfaces below (mirrors millbind's yard_board precedent for post/bore-style engagement). Nothing on the shell overhangs its own 29mm footprint, so a seated shell never fouls a neighbouring pan's contents.

parts.name: spine
parts.notes: The common supply of quills -- 24 total, six per seat at a full table (idea.json's own figures). bbox x/y=11mm uses the stated blade thickness ('~11mm thick') as the piece's widest footprint. bbox z=32mm RECONCILES three figures idea.json gives for this piece that do not sum consistently on their own: a '6mm peg 12mm long', a blade '~13mm long', and the whole piece 'standing ~20mm proud of the shell' (12+13=25, not 20). I read the 12mm peg as fully buried flush in the shell's 12mm-deep socket (the two figures match exactly, so this is the more load-bearing pair), took the stated '~20mm proud' as the authoritative EXPOSED height above the shell surface (it is the number idea.json itself uses for the grasp/pinch ergonomics -- 'chunky enough to pinch out'), and read the '~13mm long' blade figure as describing only the tapered wedge-tipped upper portion of that 20mm rather than an independent additional length (see unstated_in_spec). Total standalone height = 12mm (buried peg) + 20mm (exposed quill) = 32mm. Seated in a shell socket it stands vertically, its POSITION near one of the shell's six face centres (not an angled blade) being what 'points... at one neighbouring pan' -- a vertical peg keeps every spine printable with no supports and matches the socket being 'sunk vertically'. Stays wholly inside the shell's own 29mm footprint (no overhang).

parts.name: pearl_one_ring
parts.notes: The common grade. Smooth domed knob ~16mm across and ~11mm tall on a plain round 6mm shaft ~16mm long (all idea.json's own stated figures) -- bbox x/y=16mm is the knob diameter (the piece's widest feature everywhere it can be seen); bbox z=27mm is the direct sum of knob height (11mm) and shaft length (16mm), idea.json's own two figures, no invention needed. The only marking anywhere on the piece is a single 1.2mm raised ring on the flat foot of the shaft (idea.json's stated relief figure) -- readable only once the pearl is stood foot-up in a pearl_rack well; everywhere else in the game (reef pan, shell socket) that foot faces down and is hidden, by design.

parts.name: pearl_two_ring
parts.notes: The middle grade. idea.json states this piece is 'identical to pearl_one_ring in every visible respect'; two concentric 1.2mm raised rings mark the foot instead of one. Same bbox and relief_mm as pearl_one_ring for exactly that reason -- see pearl_one_ring's notes for the dimensional reasoning, not restated here.

parts.name: pearl_three_ring
parts.notes: The rare grade. idea.json states this piece is 'identical to pearl_one_ring in every visible respect'; three concentric 1.2mm raised rings mark the foot instead of one. Same bbox and relief_mm as pearl_one_ring -- see pearl_one_ring's notes.

parts.name: pearl_rack
parts.notes: Landing rack, ~135 x 34 x 22mm (idea.json's own stated figures, used directly), barnacle-stippled skirt (1.2mm relief, idea.json's stated figure). Six round wells, 17mm across and 9mm deep, each with a thumb scallop (idea.json's own explicit figures -- a genuine 'whole piece drops into a pocket' seat, unlike the peg-only reef_board/urchin_shell sockets, and a direct match for the `cut_wells` block, which builds a thumb scallop in by default). recesses.holds='pearl_one_ring' is REPRESENTATIVE for all three pearl grades, which idea.json states are dimensionally identical -- the same six wells accept any grade interchangeably; a pearl is dropped in knob-down, its shaft (16mm) standing proud above the well, its ringed foot -- the only marking in the game -- finally readable. Clearance = (17-16)/2 = 0.5mm per side (idea.json's own 17mm well over its own 16mm knob, no invention). One end carries a triangular, square, pentagonal or hexagonal prism finial matching that seat's urchin_shell knob (a cosmetic identity match between two DIFFERENT parts, not a mechanical mate, so no `joins` interface is declared for it). Six wells is a hard capacity, per idea.json's own rule text.

parts.name: tide_pot
parts.notes: The supply vessel: a deep blind drum ~85mm across and ~95mm tall (idea.json's stated figures) with an open scalloped tray ~150mm across moulded around its foot (idea.json's stated figure). bbox x/y=150mm uses the tray's own stated width, since it is the widest feature of the whole part; bbox z=95mm uses the drum's own stated height, since idea.json gives no reason to think the shallow foot-tray adds to it (see unstated_in_spec). 1.2mm barnacle stipple on the drum body (idea.json's stated relief figure). Used at setup to shake and blind-draw the 16 pearls, and through play as the open, shared spine supply tray -- a loose bulk store, not a fitted seat for any one piece, so no `recesses` block (mirrors millbind's granary_bin and yard_board loose-supply precedent).

interfaces.notes: Every one of the 37 pan dishes seats any urchin_shell -- a 30mm hex dish over a 29mm hex shell, 0.5mm clearance per side (idea.json's own explicit figure, arithmetically exact against its own 30mm/29mm figures, no invention). reef_board OWNS the 30mm dish width; urchin_shell's 29mm footprint is idea.json's own separately-stated figure and the two already agree exactly, so nothing here needed reconciling. The hex-on-hex geometry indexes a shell to one of six 60-degree orientations on re-seating, which is how the TURN action reads structurally: lift clear of the dish (full clearance, no drag), rotate in the air, set back down into the same symmetric pocket.

spine's 6mm, 12mm-long peg fully occupies one of urchin_shell's 6.6mm-diameter, 12mm-deep sockets, flush to the socket floor (both idea.json's own explicit figures). Clearance = (6.6-6)/2 = 0.3mm per side -- FLAGGED TOLERANCE: tighter than this pipeline's usual 0.4mm minimum seat clearance, but both 6.6mm and 6mm are idea.json's own explicit numbers, not approximations, so they are kept as stated rather than loosened (same practice as millbind's pin/bore joints). Spines are inserted and withdrawn constantly (GROW, SHED, ROB), so this is a repeated-use slip joint, not a one-time press fit -- a build that comes out tighter than 0.3mm/side in practice should be treated as a print-tolerance failure, not a spec ambiguity.

interfaces.joint: shaft-into-socket, partial engagement (12mm of a 16mm shaft)
interfaces.notes: REPRESENTATIVE for all three pearl grades (identical shaft geometry). A pearl carried in a shell (TAKE, ROB, DROP-in-progress) sits shaft-down in an empty socket exactly like a spine's peg, same 6.6mm bore and the same flagged 0.3mm/side clearance -- but the shaft (16mm) is longer than the socket (12mm deep), so 4mm of shaft stands exposed above the shell's socket mouth before the 16mm knob rests on it. This is the SAME socket spine uses (one bore size serves both piece families by design, per idea.json's own rule that a socket can hold either).

interfaces.joint: shaft-into-pan-socket, partial engagement (10mm of a 16mm shaft)
interfaces.notes: REPRESENTATIVE for all three pearl grades. A pearl standing directly on the reef (setup blind-plant, or the DROP action) seats its 6mm shaft into a pan's 6.6mm-diameter, 10mm-deep centre socket (both idea.json's own explicit figures) -- 6mm of shaft stands exposed above the pan floor before the knob rests on it. Same flagged 0.3mm/side clearance as the shell sockets, kept as stated for the same reason.

REPRESENTATIVE for all three pearl grades (idea.json states them dimensionally identical). A pearl stood knob-down in a 17mm, 9mm-deep well -- 0.5mm clearance per side, both idea.json's own figures, arithmetically exact, no invention. This is the one moment in the whole game a pearl's grade is visible, and the only genuine 'whole piece drops into a pocket' seat in the brief -- everywhere else a pearl only ever engages a socket by its shaft (see the `joins` entries above).

print_plan.notes:
No part exceeds the 246 x 246 x 251mm P2S bed once reef_board is read corner-to-corner (238 x 206 x 14mm, see reef_board's own notes and unstated_in_spec) -- a single tile, no dovetail joins needed anywhere in this brief. reef_board prints floor-down: all 37 pan dishes, their 1.2mm ripple floors, the 19 seed collars, the 6 landing barnacle clusters, and the 37 centre sockets are all top-face cuts/reliefs, no supports. The 37-point hex-radial lattice (centre + 3 rings at 34mm pitch) needs a HAND-ROLLED generator, not `shared_positions` (that block is a rectangular cols x rows helper and does not produce a hex-radial ring pattern) -- but the same discipline applies by hand: generate the 37 positions once and reuse that exact list for the dish cuts, the centre-socket cuts, and the seed/landing relief overlays, never regenerate the lattice trig a second time. urchin_shell prints dome-up or dome-down (whichever is flatter to the bed -- likely socket-openings-down is impractical since sockets are open pockets on the dome's upper face; print dome resting on its knob-and-rim, socket openings facing up, all six sockets and the radial dome grooves are then straightforward top-face cuts, no supports). spine prints peg-down, blade up -- a short vertical peg into a stouter vertical wedge, self-supporting, no supports needed. pearl_one_ring / pearl_two_ring / pearl_three_ring print knob-down, shaft-up (or the reverse; either is a simple axisymmetric print), with the ring relief cut into the flat foot as a straightforward end-face engraving, no supports. pearl_rack prints well-side up, flat on its skirt -- `cut_wells` is a direct match here (round wells, thumb scallop on by default) and should be used for all 6 wells per rack, all four racks sharing one call with the finial swapped per player. tide_pot prints foot-down, drum opening up, with the scalloped tray moulded around the base as a simple outward flare from the same print -- no supports.

blocks.py notes for the builder: use `add_piece_family` for every multi-copy family -- 4x urchin_shell, 24x spine, 8x pearl_one_ring, 5x pearl_two_ring, 3x pearl_three_ring, 4x pearl_rack -- each copy must land as a separately named assembly child, per the lesson graduated from the 48-tile/65-piece union failure; nothing in this brief should ever be unioned into one body. `seated_pair` is not a direct fit for the peg/socket joints here (its default free-fit formula assumes a press-fit pocket being derived FROM the piece, whereas idea.json states both the peg/shaft nominal (6mm) AND the socket diameter (6.6mm) explicitly and independently) -- its underlying discipline still applies: reef_board OWNS the 30mm dish width for the one true `recesses` seat in this brief, and every other dimension in this file derives from, or is checked against, an explicitly-stated pair rather than being restated as a second independent number.

unstated_in_spec: reef_board's '~238mm across the flats' is read as the board's overall CORNER-TO-CORNER span, not the literal flat-to-flat measurement the phrase names. This is the only reading consistent with the board's own pitch/ring/pan-size numbers (34mm pitch x 3 rings + a pan's own 17.3mm circumradius = 238.6mm corner-to-corner, matching almost exactly) and with idea.json's own claim that the board fits the P2S bed in one piece (a literal flat-to-flat=238mm reading implies a 274.8mm corner-to-corner, which fails the 246mm bed at every rotation -- the best-case minimal bounding square across all rotations works out to ~265mm). Derived flat-to-flat (bbox y) = 238 x sqrt(3)/2 = 206.1mm, rounded to 206mm.

urchin_shell's total standalone height (34mm) is my additive reading of two figures idea.json states as separate features without a combined total: the '~18mm tall' dome body and the grip knob that 'rises ~16mm for lifting' out of the dome's crown. I read the knob as standing further proud of the 18mm dome (18+16=34) rather than being subsumed within it.

spine's total standalone height (32mm) reconciles three figures that do not sum on their own: a 12mm peg, a '~13mm long' blade, and 'standing ~20mm proud of the shell' (12+13=25, not 20). I read the 12mm peg as fully buried flush in the shell's 12mm-deep socket, took the stated 20mm proud figure as the authoritative exposed height (it is the number idea.json itself uses for pinch/grasp ergonomics), and read the 13mm blade figure as describing only the wedge-tipped upper portion of that 20mm rather than an additional independent length.

tide_pot's open scalloped foot-tray is given a width (~150mm) but no separate height; I treated it as shallow enough not to add to the drum's own stated 95mm overall height, since idea.json gives no figure suggesting otherwise.

The 0.3mm-per-side clearance on every peg/socket and shaft/socket joint (6.6mm socket over a 6mm peg or shaft) is tighter than this pipeline's usual 0.4mm minimum seat clearance. Both numbers are idea.json's own explicit figures, not approximations, so I kept them as stated and flagged the tolerance in each `joins` interface's notes rather than loosening either one (same practice as millbind's pin/bore joints).
